The core insight is that oddsmakers, despite aiming for balanced betting, introduce systematic biases into spread setting. These biases reflect latent information about game outcomes but are not fully optimized due to cognitive or algorithmic limitations. By modeling these biases as a stochastic kernel, we derive a predictive framework where spread entropy serves as a proxy for information content. In GSI, this translates to Bayesian updating on outcome likelihoods conditioned on spread bias. In GSE, it maps to state transitions where entropy minimization drives strategic inference. The failure mode occurs when entropy exceeds 1.0 bit, indicating that spread no longer reliably reflects outcome probabilities, rendering the bias kernel ineffective.
